rationale: Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The seven raws explicitly encode A-to-B permeability divided by B-to-A permeability. It is retained because existing transport, flux, inverse-direction efflux, and brain/blood permeability ratios change either the measurement basis, matrix, or direction.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The raw `Cb/Cp and CCSF/Cp` is the same brain-and-CSF relative-to-plasma endpoint family already represented by `brain_csf_to_plasma_ratio` (7 assignments); the terminal existing representative outranks this one-assignment spelling.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. All four raws specify peak/maximum brain concentration relative to plasma concentration. Existing retained `brain_cmax_to_plasma_ratio` has the same numerator point type and an intentionally unspecified plasma-concentration denominator, with 13 assignments.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The three raws jointly report an absolute brain concentration and a brain/plasma ratio. This composite is retained because neither a concentration-only nor ratio-only label preserves both measurements.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The raw jointly reports an unspecified brain concentration and an explicitly unbound brain concentration. It is retained rather than promoted to total-plus-unbound because the first component is not explicitly total.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. This is an intra-arterial-versus-intravenous brain-concentration comparison. It is retained separately from the existing route ratio because the raw does not state division.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. This is an intravenous-versus-intracerebroventricular brain-concentration comparison. No existing endpoint preserves both routes without converting the comparison into a ratio.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The three raws state knockout-versus-wild-type brain-concentration comparisons but do not state division. It remains distinct from KO/WT ratios, fold changes, radioactivity, and exposure comparisons.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The raw describes the percentage of compounds concentrated in brain. It is retained as the count-tied, lexically preferred concentration-percentage label and is not interchangeable with penetration, extraction, or dose percentage.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The raw is a phenotype comparison of brain-tissue concentrations. It remains distinct from genotype, route, ischemia, ratio, and fold-change endpoints.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The raw is ordinary brain concentration divided by maximum plasma concentration. Existing retained `brain_to_peak_plasma_ratio` has the same asymmetric point semantics and 7 assignments.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The numerator is a point brain concentration while the denominator is integrated plasma exposure. It is retained because point/AUC asymmetry must not be collapsed into ordinary brain/plasma exposure or concentration ratios.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The two raws describe non-percentage dose per gram specifically in brain. It is retained as the intended brain-specific representative and remains distinct from generic tissue dose, amount, and percent-injected-dose labels.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The raw is drug percentage normalized to 0.01 g of brain. Its explicit mass scale is retained rather than merged with per-gram or unnormalized brain percentages.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The numerator is brain exposure while the denominator is plasma point concentration. It is retained because exposure/concentration asymmetry differs from AUC/AUC and concentration/concentration ratios.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The raw reports a fraction, not a percentage, of administered dose in brain. It remains distinct from percent administered/injected dose and concentration-per-dose endpoints.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. This is gadolinium amount per gram of brain normalized again by administered dose. No other catalog label preserves analyte, brain mass normalization, and administered-dose normalization together.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. Injected dose per gram of brain is the same non-percentage brain dose-per-mass endpoint as retained targeted representative `brain_dose_per_g` (2 assignments); the lower-count spelling merges there.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The raw compares brain-metastasis and normal-brain concentrations without stating division. It remains distinct from metastasis/normal ratios and absolute metastasis concentrations.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The 26 raws consistently report percent injected dose per gram specifically in brain. It is retained as the highest-count brain-specific representative, rather than losing matrix to a generic tissue label.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The raw reports percent injected dose per brain volume (cc). It remains distinct from per-gram brain values and generic-tissue per-mL values because matrix and normalization basis are protected.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. Brain percentage of injected dose is synonymous with existing retained `percent_id_in_brain` (2 assignments); the latter is the higher-count terminal representative with the same matrix and dose basis.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The raw gives a generic percentage per gram of brain without identifying injected dose. It is retained rather than adding unsupported ID/dose semantics or changing its mass normalization.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. All 13 raws explicitly leave brain-versus-plasma numerator direction unspecified. It is retained rather than forcing brain/plasma or plasma/brain direction, or converting a ratio to a general relationship.

Compared against all 8,259 refreshed catalog labels. The seven raws jointly or alternatively report brain/plasma AUC and Cmax ratios. It is retained as the highest-count explicit AUC/Cmax family and is not collapsed into either an AUC-only or Cmax-only endpoint.
